issues.description: The problem statement and the reference solution specify that construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...) should return a stim.Circuit, but the template function is annotated to return None. This conflicting return-type annotation (and the template raising NotImplementedError rather than returning a Circuit when implemented) can confuse students about whether they should construct and return a stim.Circuit or modify the provided circuit in-place. It may also cause static type-checkers or autograders that inspect return values to behave unexpectedly.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template function signature consistent with the problem statement and the solution by changing the return annotation to -> stim.Circuit and ensuring the docstring/signature agree. Specifically, in template_repository/msd.py update the signature to: def construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(Hx: npt.NDArray[np.int8], offset: int = 0) -> stim.Circuit: and keep the docstring stating it returns a stim.Circuit. This removes ambiguity about whether students should return a Circuit and aligns the template with the reference solution.
